name: 01 Exchange Grants
description: In collaboration with the Solana Foundation, is open to everyone in the community, and provides on-going opportunities to contribute to the 01 and Solana ecosystem

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The 01 Exchange grants program, in collaboration with the Solana Foundation, is open to everyone in the community, and provides on-going opportunities to contribute to the 01 and Solana ecosystem.
Reach out to the team through the official grant request channel before starting any grant.
Unless specified otherwise, only one person/ team can win a grant.
Submissions will be accepted for each grant up to 2 weeks after the first person submits a satisfactory entry.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: After this point, the team will decide which submitted entry wins based on quality of work.
Build a strategy vault that generates yield by running a delta neutral strategy on 01.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: The vault should run a delta neutral trading strategy on any 01 Exchange market - The vault should be launched publicly to mainnet - The vault should have an accessible frontend interface.

The vault should run a funding arbitrage trading strategy on any 01 Exchange market, and another exchange - The vault should be launched publicly to mainnet - The vault should have an accessible frontend interface.
Pub/Sub to select markets and receive real-time data - Real-time L2/L3 data - Real-time trade orders - Open Sourced

The CLI should be able to do the following: 1) Open margin account 2) Place orders 3) Cancel orders 4) Settle funds 5) Liquidate another account 6) Deposit/ Withdraw/ Borrow 7) View account balance/ risk 8) View positions - The CLI should be open sourced
Make a tweet every time someone get’s liquidated for a medium-large size on 01 - The tweet should describe the trade position, the entry price, the liquidation price, the market, and the leverage
Make a tweet every time there is a cross-exchange arbitrage opportunity between 01 and another exchange - Detail the arbitrage, and the potential extractable value
Make a tweet every time a market order with a size larger than $100,000 is placed on any market - Detail the trader’s key, the order size, the market, and the entry price
Make a tweet every day with the current borrow and lending rates on 01 for all assets

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official 01 Exchange Grants portal at https://01exchange.notion.site/01-Exchange-Grants-Program-ecbab6fde93843caa6924fb5cda3b79e. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

name: 0G Foundation Ecosystem Growth Program
description: The 0G Foundation Ecosystem Growth Program provides milestone-based funding, compute subsidies, and technical support for teams building modular AI data availability, storage, and alignment networks.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: 0G is a modular AI blockchain architecture featuring an ultra-high-throughput data availability layer and decentralized storage network. The Ecosystem Growth Program backs builders solving the AI data bottleneck.

Selected projects receive capital grants, compute resource subsidies, and architectural guidance to deploy data-heavy applications, onchain AI agents, and verifiable inference protocols directly on 0G infrastructure.

sections.heading: Target focus areas
bullets: High-throughput data availability integrations for Layer 2 rollups and application-specific execution layers.
Decentralized storage solutions for massive multimodal AI datasets, model weights, and verifiable training checkpoints.
Autonomous onchain AI agents, model alignment networks, and decentralized inference verification pipelines.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your proposal via the 0G Foundation ecosystem portal. Include a technical architecture whitepaper, repository links, benchmark data availability requirements, and planned mainnet deployment milestones.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: 1Password for Startups
amount: Free 1Password Teams for open source projects
description: 1Password relies on open source software every day. It's fair to say that 1Password wouldn't exist without the open source community, so we want to give back and help teams be more productive and secure.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Are you working on an open source project?
Do you need a place to securely store and share your project's login credentials, API tokens, SSH keys, database information, and other secrets?
Somewhere that also allows you to use them right in your development workflow?
1Password has your back: get a free Teams account on us.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: When you join the program, you'll get a free 1Password Teams account.
Here's what you can expect:

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Your membership doesn't expire as long as your project remains eligible for the program.
The whole team can use 1Password, everywhere: Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, Linux, and in the browser.

Developers can integrate 1Password into their development workflows, including managing SSH keys and signing Git commits, authenticating CLIs with biometrics, and securing secrets throughout your projects.
You must be an owner of your team account to apply. Don't have an account? Start a 14 day trial.
To decrease the chances of getting locked out of your account, invite at least one other person to your team and add them to the Owners group.
Apply by completing this form and opening a new issue in this repository.

Only team accounts are eligible for this program. Personal, family, and business accounts are not currently eligible for the program. If you want to maintain your current account and apply to the program, consider changing your account type.

Your 1Password account must not be associated with commercial activity, with the exception of open source funding programs like GitHub Sponsorships or Open Collective. If your company is looking for an enterprise password manager, check out 1Password Business.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official 1Password for Startups portal at https://github.com/1Password/for-open-source. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

name: 3327 Grants
description: We support the teams and individuals building solutions for the web of tomorrow

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: One could say we are a DAO, but without all the buzz and hype.
we are probably what DAOs could become eventually.

fully functional collectives with the shared vision, passion, and principles, where responsibility, accountability, gains, and profits for the work done are shared among team members, rather than just a few at the top.
One way or the other, we are an open collective that invites people who share an enthusiasm for technology and innovation to join our distributed team.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: The only thing we are not looking for at 3327 are middlemen of all kinds.
Apply by sending a link to your CV, what drives you, and what got you excited about 3327 via a message at 3327.eth on Rinkeby Testnet.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Strong proficiency in React and ES6 (Typescript is a big plus)
Excellent understanding of Javascript Web3 libraries like ethers.js
Excellent understanding of libraries for connecting wallets with the UI
Excellent understanding of UI state management (for example Redux), function components and hooks
Ability to write tests (for example Cypress, JEST)

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your proposal through the official 3327 Grants application portal at https://3327.io/contribute/#project-grants-report. Detail your technical architecture, open-source repository, and milestone roadmap.

name: Aave Grants
description: Aave Grants DAO funds community ideas that grow the Aave ecosystem through milestone grants reviewed on a rolling basis.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Aave Grants DAO is funded through Aave DAO governance and supports developers, integrations, audits, and community programs that strengthen the protocol.
Applications are reviewed monthly with no fixed cohort deadline.

Applicants should demonstrate clear technical feasibility, active development cadence, and open-source documentation. Deliverables are evaluated against predefined milestones before grant capital or platform credits are disbursed.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs: What is Aave Grants DAO? It is a community grants program focused on growing the Aave ecosystem by funding vetted ideas, projects, and teams.
Does AGD fund Lens grants? No. Lens runs a separate grants process through Aave Companies.
How do I claim milestone payments? Use the official claim form linked from AGD after each approved milestone is delivered.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit a rolling application on aavegrants.org. You should receive a response within about one month.
Check your inbox for “Congratulations & AGD Next Steps” to confirm receipt; follow up through official AGD channels if you have not heard back after one month.

name: Abey Foundation
description: The Abey Foundation Grants Program awards non-dilutive, milestone-based funding to developers and teams building high-throughput dApps, cross-chain DeFi, and interoperability tools on ABEYChain.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: ABEYChain is a hybrid PoW/DPoS blockchain designed for high transaction throughput and cross-chain composability. The Abey Foundation Grants Program fuels ecosystem expansion across decentralized finance and gaming.
Grant recipients receive non-dilutive capital alongside direct technical assistance from core protocol developers, security audit subsidies, and exchange listing and community visibility support.

sections.heading: What reviewers look for
bullets: Decentralized exchanges, lending protocols, and structured financial products leveraging ABEYChain speed.
Cross-chain bridges, asset wrapping mechanisms, and oracle integrations connecting ABEY with other major chains.
Web3 gaming ecosystems, NFT marketplaces, and enterprise data solutions demonstrating live user traction.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply through the Abey Foundation grants portal with your team background, functional prototype or testnet deployment, smart contract audit status, and detailed milestone delivery schedule.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Acala Network Grants
description: Acala Network Grants fund developers building cross-chain DeFi protocols, liquid staking derivatives, and financial infrastructure within the Polkadot and Kusama cross-consensus ecosystems.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Acala serves as the decentralized liquidity hub of Polkadot. The Acala Grants Program fosters innovative financial primitives that utilize Acala’s EVM+ environment and native cross-consensus messaging (XCM).

The program distributes milestone-based funding to open-source builders creating decentralized stablecoin applications, liquid staking integrations (LDOT), automated market makers, and cross-chain yield aggregators.

sections.heading: Key funding tracks
bullets: EVM+ compatible smart contract dApps bringing novel lending, trading, and asset management models to Polkadot.
Cross-chain infrastructure utilizing Polkadot XCM for seamless multi-parachain asset transfers and shared liquidity.
Developer tooling including indexers, analytics dashboards, and automated SDKs for Acala protocol interaction.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit a formal grant proposal on the Acala GitHub grants repository or official ecosystem portal. Proposals must include open-source code repositories, measurable milestone deliverables, and budget breakdowns.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Aethir Ecosystem Fund
description: Aethir’s ecosystem fund backs teams building decentralized AI compute, gaming, and agent workloads on Aethir infrastructure, including accelerator cohorts with NEAR and Delphi Labs.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The fund targets projects that need GPU-class decentralized compute rather than centralized cloud credits alone. Awards are sized per project scope, with published tiers between roughly $5,000 and $500,000 for teams that demonstrate traction on Aethir or partner networks.
Premier partners such as NEAR Foundation may co-sponsor accelerator tracks where accepted teams receive compute, mentorship, and go-to-market introductions alongside capital.

sections.heading: What reviewers look for
bullets: Live or near-live workloads that route inference, training, or rendering through decentralized compute.
Open roadmaps that explain user growth, unit economics, and how additional compute unlocks the next milestone.
Teams that can publish reproducible benchmarks or usage metrics after each funding tranche.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Start from Aethir’s ecosystem fund page and follow the current application or partner accelerator link. Include architecture diagrams, expected GPU hours, and milestone dates so reviewers can match you to the right award band.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Aethir x Polyhedra Grant Program
description: The Aethir x Polyhedra Grant Program provides compute allocations and zero-knowledge infrastructure grants to teams developing high-performance ZK-ML, web3 gaming, and cross-chain AI systems.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Aethir and Polyhedra Network have partnered to accelerate teams at the intersection of decentralized GPU computing and zero-knowledge cryptography. The joint grant addresses compute bottlenecks for proving systems.

Recipients obtain enterprise-grade NVIDIA GPU cluster hours from Aethir combined with Polyhedra’s zkBridge and zero-knowledge proving algorithms to build verifiable artificial intelligence and scalable gaming worlds.

sections.heading: Eligible project tracks
bullets: Zero-knowledge machine learning (ZK-ML) pipelines requiring high-throughput GPU clusters for proof generation.
Cross-chain interoperability protocols and interoperable game assets verified via Polyhedra zkBridge.
Decentralized AI agents and verifiable inference applications demanding high compute density and cryptographic validity.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply via the Aethir ecosystem program intake channel. Provide system architecture specs, anticipated monthly GPU hours, proof-generation benchmarks, and target mainnet integration timelines.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Agentic Engineering Grants
description: Ideas → Prompt → Prod TL;DR: The barrier to building software has collapsed. This grant gives you $200 USDG to access a month of the highest tier of AI coding tools so you can build and ship something meaningful on Solana. Approved builders receive 50% upfront and 50% upon shipping.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Ideas → Prompt → Prod TL;DR: The barrier to building software has collapsed.
This grant gives you $200 USDG to access a month of the highest tier of AI coding tools so you can build and ship something meaningful on Solana.
Approved builders receive 50% upfront and 50% upon shipping.
The Hypothesis For the first time, building software is no longer gated by technical skill but by ideas and agency.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: AI coding tools have compressed weeks of work into hours.
The people who win in this environment are the ones who have something they want to build, take initiative, and actually ship.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Ideas → Prompt → Prod TL;DR: The barrier to building software has collapsed. This grant gives you $200 USDG to access a month of the highest tier of AI coding tools so you can build and ship something meaningful on Solana. Approved builders receive 50% upfront and 50% upon shipping. The Hypothesis For the first time, building software is no longer gated by technical skill but by ideas and agency. AI coding tools have compressed weeks of work into hours. The people who win in this environment are the ones who have something they want to build, take initiative, and actually ship. This grant is a small nudge in that direction: give you access to a powerful coding tool at the right moment and help you turn an idea into a shipped Solana product. You get $200 USDG to cover an AI coding Pro subscription. 50% upfront, 50% after you've shipped. The only requirement is that it should be a working Solana product. How It Works Apply on Superteam Earn with a clear description of what you want to build and how you'll use AI tools. If approved, you'll receive 50% of the grant upfront (post KYC; to be done on this page on Earn) in the following weekly payout cycle. Approved KYC and payments are sent for processing on Mondays and paid to you by Friday of the same week. From there, you build and ship. After your product/MVP is live, share your project's URL, GitHub repo, and upload your coding subscription receipt(s) to the tranche application form on this listing — the totals shown in the receipt(s) should be $200. This tranche application form will be visible to you after you have received your first tranche. Upon review and approval, you will receive the leftover 50% of the grant. What We're Looking For The scope in your application form should be clear and practical (read: shippable). Your idea/project should have some Solana integration. A live, working product/MVP at the time of your second tranche application. While open-source repos are encouraged, you may keep your repo private. If you decide to close-source your code, you are required to share access with abhwshek@gmail.com so that we can review the code. Questions? Reach out to support@superteam.fun for help.

name: Airtable for Startups
description: Airtable for Startups awards early-stage founders up to $2,000 in platform credits to build automated relational workflows, product roadmaps, and custom internal operations hubs.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Airtable for Startups helps fast-moving teams organize operations, investor relations, content pipelines, and customer feedback without engineering custom internal tools.

Approved ventures receive credit packages valid for Team or Business plan subscriptions, unlocking unlimited automated workflows, relational table linking, interactive interface designer dashboards, and advanced permissioning.

sections.heading: Core startup benefits
bullets: Up to $2,000 in software credits applicable across Airtable Team and Business annual subscriptions.
Interface Designer access to create tailor-made internal dashboards for team members and external stakeholders.
Pre-built startup operational templates covering fundraising pipelines, sprint planning, and applicant tracking.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply through the Airtable startup portal using your corporate email address and details of your startup accelerator or venture capital backing. Verified accounts receive credits within three business days.
Submissions are verified directly against partner registry databases. Once approved, credit codes and tier upgrades are provisioned directly to your company administrative account.

name: Airwallex for Startups
description: Airwallex for Startups offers venture-backed companies up to $50,000 in fee-free foreign exchange transfers, multi-currency corporate cards, and international payment infrastructure.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Airwallex for Startups simplifies cross-border financial operations for global teams. The program eliminates banking friction by providing virtual accounts across 60+ countries and zero-fee foreign currency conversions.

Founders access competitive global FX rates, issue physical and virtual employee corporate debit cards with built-in expense management, and integrate seamless payment collection APIs for international customers.

sections.heading: Program perks & features
bullets: Up to $50,000 in fee-free foreign exchange volume across major global currencies including USD, EUR, GBP, and SGD.
Free corporate multi-currency cards with customizable spend limits, real-time receipt capture, and Xero sync.
Dedicated startup onboarding specialist and prioritized customer support for high-volume cross-border payments.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Register via the Airwallex startup partnership page with proof of venture capital backing or startup community membership. Once corporate KYC is completed, FX waiver credits are applied automatically.
Submissions are verified directly against partner registry databases. Once approved, credit codes and tier upgrades are provisioned directly to your company administrative account.

name: Akash Grants
description: We invest in the people who build the roads. If you are developing open-source tools, infrastructure, or specialized interfaces for the Akash Network, the grant program provides the capital to fund your development.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Smaller contributions drive the network's daily momentum.
Through community-governed funding, AKT is available for developers and creators helping build documentation, manage testnets, or develop content.
Whether you are fixing a bug in the Akash Console or launching a pilot program, the community matches network needs with your specific skill set.
Show up, contribute, and earn as the protocol matures.

Applicants should demonstrate clear technical feasibility, active development cadence, and open-source documentation. Deliverables are evaluated against predefined milestones before grant capital or platform credits are disbursed.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: The Akash community pool is a permissionless funding source for the network.
Any individual or team can request capital for any project, at any scale, provided the proposal passes on-chain governance.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: The Akash community pool is a permissionless funding source for the network. Any individual or team can request capital for any project, at any scale, provided the proposal passes on-chain governance.

name: Alchemy-Arbitrum Grant Program
description: Alchemy has launched a $10M grant program to support Orbit chain development. The program offers up to $500K in Alchemy infrastructure credits for teams building or migrating to Orbit-based rollups.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Alchemy and Arbitrum run a $10 million credits program for teams launching or migrating Orbit-based rollups. Approved builders can receive up to $500,000 in Alchemy infrastructure credits to offset node, API, and developer platform costs while they scale.
The grant is designed so infrastructure cost does not block experimentation with dedicated app chains and custom sequencing strategies.
Credits apply to first-party Alchemy services during testnet and early mainnet operations; teams should model expected RPC volume before requesting the upper award tier.

sections.heading: What credits cover
bullets: Alchemy APIs, nodes, and developer tooling used while bootstrapping an Orbit chain.
Migration support when moving an existing rollup to the Orbit stack.
Hands-on guidance from Alchemy ecosystem teams during early mainnet operations.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit the application on Alchemy’s Arbitrum grant page with your chain design, milestones, and expected infrastructure usage. Reviewers evaluate technical feasibility and ecosystem impact before allocating credits.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Alchemy Grants
description: We're committing $25 million to help developers continue building DeFi protocols, NFT experiences, or any project that helps bring web3 to the world

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Alchemy credits and dedicated engineering support for qualified teams.
Focus on your product, not your infrastructure.
Credits, support, and world-class infrastructure to go from idea to production.
Credits applied directly to your account, offsetting infrastructure costs so you can stretch your runway further.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: Compute, storage, and databases on AWS.
covered while you focus on finding product-market fit.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Who can join the Alchemy Startup Program? Any team building onchain. Whether you're VC-backed, in an accelerator, or bootstrapping your first project, we want to hear from you if you're building something real.

What are the benefits of the program? Qualified teams receive Alchemy credits, $5,000 in AWS credits, 24/7 engineering support, a dedicated onboarding experience, and access to our partner ecosystem of VCs, accelerators, and chain partners.
How do I apply? Fill out the form at the top of this page. it takes 30 seconds. Our team will review your submission and schedule a call to discuss next steps.

How do credits work? Alchemy credits are applied directly to your account and offset the cost of your plan, whether you're on pay-as-you-go or enterprise. They're automatically applied to future invoices.

Are current Alchemy customers eligible? If you're an existing customer affiliated with one of our partners, you may be eligible for additional benefits. Submit the form and our team will review your account.
I'm a VC or accelerator. can I refer my portfolio? Yes. We offer enhanced benefits for portfolio companies referred by our partners. Contact us to set up a dedicated program for your fund.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: No pitch decks, no lengthy applications. Fill out the form, get qualified by our team, and credits will hit your account within days.

name: Aleo Ecosystem Grants
description: Aleo Ecosystem Grants distribute $10,000 to $100,000+ in non-dilutive funding to developers building privacy-preserving zero-knowledge applications and Leo smart contracts on the Aleo network.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Aleo uses zero-knowledge cryptography (zkSNARKs) to provide complete programmability with absolute transactional privacy. The Aleo Grants Program funds builders who leverage zero-knowledge proofs to protect user data.

Grants are awarded across multiple tiers: Ignite Grants for early prototypes ($10K-$20K), Launch Grants for production dApps ($50K+), and Blueprint Grants for complex core protocol infrastructure and tooling.

sections.heading: Priority development categories
bullets: Private DeFi applications including dark pools, compliant private lending, and confidential automated market makers.
Zero-knowledge digital identity verification (zk-KYC), verifiable credentials, and decentralized anonymous voting.
Developer infrastructure, testing harnesses, Leo language libraries, and browser wallet proving extensions.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your proposal through the Aleo Grants portal. Include your GitHub repository, architecture overview, proof-of-concept code written in Leo or AVM instructions, and a multi-stage milestone roadmap.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Aleph Zero Ecosystem Funding Program
description: The Aleph Zero Ecosystem Funding Program allocates capital, technical advisory, and incubation to builders launching privacy-first decentralized applications on the Aleph Zero blockchain.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Aleph Zero is an enterprise-ready, high-speed Proof-of-Stake public network utilizing zero-knowledge proofs and secure Multi-Party Computation (sMPC) via its privacy framework, Liminal.

The $50M Ecosystem Funding Program provides non-dilutive grants, follow-on venture introductions, and architectural reviews to teams building private financial primitives, gaming platforms, and enterprise solutions.

sections.heading: Focus areas & review criteria
bullets: Ink! smart contracts demonstrating efficient execution, low state bloat, and comprehensive unit test coverage.
Privacy-enhanced applications combining public blockchain auditing with private user state using Liminal sMPC/ZKP.
Institutional compliance tools, private credential verification, and decentralized data custody architectures.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Complete the application form on the Aleph Zero website. Detail your product vision, tech stack, team experience with Rust/ink!, and phased deliverables. Shortlisted teams present their proposal in an interview.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Algolia for Startups
description: Algolia search credits, core search, vector search, recommend, A/B testing, personalization.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Algolia Startup Program bundles $10,000 in search and discovery credits for eligible young companies, plus perks from partner SaaS vendors and access to Algolia’s founder community.
Credits cover core search, vector search, recommend, A/B testing, and personalization APIs so you can ship discovery features without front-loading infrastructure cost.

sections.heading: Program perks
bullets: $10,000 in Algolia credits during the first 12 months after approval.
Partner credits for tools such as Datadog and Notion.
Priority support and early access to new Algolia features.
Opportunities to be featured in Algolia marketing content.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs: Who is eligible for the Algolia Startup Program? Startups under seven years old that have raised less than $15M and are not current paid Algolia customers may apply.
How much credit does an approved startup receive? Approved companies receive $10,000 in Algolia credits to use within 12 months of acceptance.
When do unused credits expire? Any unused balance lapses 12 months after approval.
What happens if we spend all credits before the 12-month window ends? Usage reverts to standard pricing. The application owner is responsible for monitoring consumption in the dashboard.
Can existing paying Algolia customers join? No. The program is limited to new or free-tier teams that meet the funding and age requirements.
Is approval guaranteed once we apply? No. Applications are reviewed against eligibility rules and product fit.
Can we apply if we previously redeemed another Algolia coupon? No. Prior coupon redemptions disqualify a team from this startup offer.
Are credits transferable? No. Credits are tied to the approved application and expire after 12 months if unused.
How do we contact the startup team? Email startups@algolia.com.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official Algolia for Startups portal at https://www.algolia.com/industries/startups. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

name: America's Seed Fund (NSF SBIR / STTR)
description: America’s Seed Fund, powered by the National Science Foundation (NSF SBIR / STTR), awards up to $2,000,000 in non-dilutive federal grants for deep-tech, cryptographic, and computational innovations.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: America’s Seed Fund is the United States government’s flagship non-dilutive funding vehicle for early-stage science and technology breakthroughs. The program operates through the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) frameworks.

Phase I awards provide up to $275,000 to conduct proof-of-concept research over 6 to 12 months. Successful projects can then apply for Phase II funding of up to $1,000,000 plus supplemental matching grants, totaling up to $2 million in non-dilutive equity-free capital.

sections.heading: Eligible research domains
bullets: Distributed ledgers, zero-knowledge proofs, and novel cryptographic protocols with national technological impact.
Artificial intelligence, verifiable computational systems, and high-performance quantum or neuromorphic architectures.
Cybersecurity infrastructure, privacy-enhancing technologies, and resilient decentralized communications.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Start by submitting a three-page Project Pitch through the NSF Seed Fund portal. If invited, prepare a formal Phase I proposal following NSF guidelines. US incorporation and majority domestic ownership are required.

name: Amplitude for Startups (Scholarship)
description: Amplitude for Startups provides early-stage teams with one year of free access to Amplitude Growth, giving builders enterprise-grade product analytics, cohort retention tracking, and conversion funnels.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Amplitude Startup Scholarship delivers up to $60,000 in software credits for venture-backed and accelerator-affiliated technology companies. Accepted teams receive full access to Amplitude Growth plan features, enabling granular user behavioral tracking across web and mobile applications.
Participants can track up to 20 million monthly events with advanced segmentation, real-time funnel analysis, customer journey mapping, and automated cohort synchronization into marketing tools.

sections.heading: Focus areas & qualification
bullets: Pre-seed to Series A technology startups that have raised under $5 million in total funding.
Teams with less than 20 employees and fewer than 2 years in operation at time of application.
Startups actively building digital web apps, onchain interfaces, or mobile products seeking product-market fit.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply directly through the Amplitude for Startups portal. Include your company domain, verification of your latest funding round or accelerator acceptance, and an overview of your current product stage. Approvals are typically processed within three business days.

name: Analog Grant Program
description: The Analog Grant Program is designed to support promising projects and community members with the objective of growing the Analog ecosystem. It rewards up to 50,000 USD (in either stablecoins or Analog tokens) in funding. with more available for exceptional cases.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: These are given to builders who connect existing smart contracts and/or runtimes on different chains through Analog, or those who use significant parts of their application code and infrastructure to query data through Analog Watch.

name: clr.fund (Clear Fund)
description: The clr.fund (Clear Fund) provides decentralized quadratic funding and matching pool allocations for developers creating Ethereum public goods, open-source infrastructure, and privacy tooling.

sections.heading: Program overview

By preventing bribery and coordinated voting through zero-knowledge proofs, clr.fund ensures that matching pool capital is distributed strictly in proportion to authentic community preference and donation count.

sections.heading: Eligible public goods
bullets: Open-source Ethereum client implementations, cryptographic libraries, developer tools, and testing environments.
Privacy-preserving protocols, zero-knowledge research, and decentralized identity governance experiments.
Public educational content, security research documentation, and open blockchain data indexing APIs.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Register your open-source project on the clr.fund platform before an active community round starts. Verify your project repository and recipient address. Community members donate directly using zk-SNARK shielded ballots.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

The COTI Builders Program funds innovative dApps across confidential DeFi, private onchain identity, decentralized state privacy, and institutional compliance that require data privacy on a public network.

name: COTI Web4 grant program
description: COTI’s Web4 grant pays autonomous agents in $COTI on a recurring 14-day cycle based on measured on-chain usage, with starter gas and open-source agent tooling.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: COTI runs usage-based grant cycles for autonomous agents rather than human application committees.
Agents earn $COTI every 14 days from a shared pool proportional to encrypted on-chain activity.
Starter gas and tooling ship through coti-skills, coti-mcp, and the private messaging SDK.

sections.heading: How it works
paragraphs: Epochs run on a 14-day cadence with a shared reward pool. Agents install skills or the SDK, claim starter gas, perform private on-chain actions, then claim proportional rewards when an epoch closes.
Usage units accrue from encrypted messaging, private transactions, and other measurable network activity published in the open-source skills repository.

sections.heading: Builder requirements
bullets: Agents must integrate through the published skills library or MCP server.
Wallets must be created or imported using the documented account-setup flow.
Teams should publish reproducible deployment steps for reviewers.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Deploy an agent using the public COTI skills repositories, then follow the starter-grant flow documented in the Web4 grant announcement linked from this page.

name: Decentralized Cloud Foundation Grants
description: Crust Grants Program, launched by the Decentralized Cloud Foundation (DCF), rewards projects that add value to the Web 3.0 decentralized cloud storage ecosystem. Crust Grants Program divides decentralized cloud storage into technology stacks at six layers, including chain protocol layer, file systems protocol layer, node strategies layer, development tools and infrastructure layer, blockchain-based applications layer and user-based applications layer. Currently, Crust Grants program mainly targets projects of protocol layer, and applications that serve a wide range of users.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: For projects whose Crust Grants application has been accepted:
Funding support up to 30,000 USDT(Small Grant $1,000 USDT);
Deep participation in the Crust technology community and the opportunity to be invited to events of Crust ecology to enhance the profile and recognition of your project;
Deep participation in Web3 ecosystem and support from Polkadot and IPFS ecosystem;

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: Crust protocol layer incentivizes and maintains a decentralized storage network.

Using IPFS as the underlying storage, it gives blockchain incentives through MPoW and GPoS protocols and provides a decentralized supply-and-demand aggregation system through DSM protocol to provide stable token incentives for storage nodes.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Changing the Bitswap mechanism to optimize the credit mechanism for data exchange, thus improving the efficiency of IPFS Retrieval (See implementation in the Bitswap codebase:https://github.com/ipfs/go-bitswap);
Providing encrypted version of IPFS. Here is the go-ipfs-encryptor codebase that Crust team is currently implementing:https://github.com/crustio/go-ipfs-encryptor;
Becoming more compatible with different decentralized storage protocols, such as adapting to DAT Project (See the codebase:https://github.com/datproject/dat)..?fileGuid=8g6KfhSut6oyB6R1)
Working on the optimal strategy about hard disk organization, including Raid mechanism optimization, hard disk management plan, etc.;
Optimizing and adapting Crust Node (See the codebase:https://github.com/crustio/crust-node);

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official Decentralized Cloud Foundation Grants portal at https://wiki.crust.network/docs/en/crustGrants. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

The platform connects with over 100 SaaS and cloud tools (AWS, GitHub, Google Workspace, Jira) to continuously audit security configurations and flag compliance gaps before formal audit reviews.

sections.heading: Core platform features
bullets: Automated evidence collection for 14+ compliance frameworks including SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR.
Comprehensive pre-built security policy templates drafted by former auditors and security compliance leaders.
Drata Trust Center to publicly demonstrate security posture, certifications, and sub-processor lists to buyers.

sections.heading: How to apply

Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply

name: Eigen Foundation Community Grants
description: For 2025, the Eigen Foundation will commit to a spending cap of 40M EIGEN, to be distributed across two Grant Initiatives: Open Innovation Grants (smaller allocations to developers and founders who drive early-stage ecosystem development) and Strategic Grants (larger, targeted allocations to high-caliber teams who drive long-term value and adoption).

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Eigen Foundation introduces its 2025 community grants strategy with 40M EIGEN tokens allocated to foster ecosystem growth through structured six-month seasons, oversight mechanisms, and transparent fund deployment.
The Eigen Foundation’s mandate is to grow the EigenLayer ecosystem and steward a network of open innovation.

With this goal in mind, 15% of the total initial EIGEN supply has been allocated toward EigenLayer community initiatives such as incentive programs and grants for users, developers, and community contributors.
Starting this year, the Eigen Foundation will steward the effective, intentional, and responsible deployment of these grants for the EigenLayer community.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: Coordinating token grants within protocol ecosystems has historically been a challenge due to the difficulty in aligning a diverse group of tokenholders on strategic growth needs while ensuring accountability for grant teams.
In practice, grants are best distributed by small, independent teams with high strategic context, allowing them to move fast and adapt quickly.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Encourage early-stage teams to build on experimental and innovative products and technologies in the EigenLayer ecosystem
Support the gradual onboarding of broader engineering participation in EigenLayer core development
Increase use cases and economy of EigenLayer, including AVSs utilizing restaking, EigenDA, and any additional primitives
Enable token-related initiatives, including liquidity and governance operations

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official Eigen Foundation Community Grants portal at https://blog.eigenfoundation.org/introducing-community-initiatives-and-grants/. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

name: Endless Education Fund
description: To further the long-term development of the Endless ecosystem and strengthen community members’ grasp of the Endless white paper, core products, and development stack, we are officially launching the Endless Education Fund. The program invites developers, researchers, educators, and content creators worldwide to contribute to Endless’s knowledge base by producing systematic, professional, and high-quality educational resources for the entire ecosystem.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Endless Education Fund invites developers, researchers, educators, and content creators to produce systematic learning materials that explain the Endless white paper, core products, and development stack.
Grants are milestone-based and aim to grow a shared knowledge base the whole ecosystem can reuse.

sections.heading: Eligible content

Video or written curricula with clear learning outcomes and licensing that allows remixing.
Localized education that expands access beyond English-speaking developer communities.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

Subsidies draw from a $1 million pool and apply to marketplace quotes rather than ad-hoc engagements arranged outside Areta.

description: Ethereum Foundation ESP backs open-source teams with direct grants, office hours, and ecosystem introductions across protocol R&D, developer experience, security, and public goods.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: ESP exists to shorten the path from credible research or tooling ideas to sustained maintenance inside the Ethereum ecosystem. Funding complements community grants and protocol governance rather than replacing them.
Grantees report progress through ESP’s published templates so other teams can build on shared libraries, specs, and audit results.

sections.heading: Focus areas
bullets: Core protocol improvements, testing, and client diversity efforts.

Security research, audits, and incident response preparedness.
Community infrastructure and coordination that keeps public goods online.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Teams typically begin with the ESP wishlist or an unsolicited proposal describing impact, maintainers, and budget. ESP publishes guidance on grant sizes and reporting expectations on the official ESP site.

name: Ethereum Foundation
description: Whether you're working on a specific project, or you're still exploring possibilities, you can connect with our team for guidance.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: ESP provides financial and non-financial support to eligible projects working to improve Ethereum.
We focus on work that strengthens Ethereum's foundations and enables future builders.
The work we support is open-source, non-commercial, and aligned with CROPS principles (Censorship Resistance, Open Source, Privacy, and Security) to create positive-sum outcomes for the community.

Our support is generally directed toward enabling builders rather than end-users: strengthening Ethereum's infrastructure, expanding the range of tools available to those building on Ethereum, gaining a deeper understanding of cryptographic primitives, growing the builder ecosystem through education and community development, etc.

sections.heading: Program details

sections.heading: How to apply

Describe how your background and approach align with the project requirements by providing clear information on your methodology, timeline, and deliverables. Once submitted, you will receive a confirmation email.

The Grant Management (GM) team reviews applications in collaboration with the EF team responsible for the corresponding Wishlist or RFP item. The evaluation process may include: an interview to discuss your proposal in detail, project rescoping, or budget negotiations.

name: Ethereum Foundation - Project Odin
description: Every so often, in the blockchain world’s usual cycle of funding scares, a team maintaining a widely used open source public good declares mayday. Libp2p is a core infrastructure stack that powers multiple Ethereum clients (among others) and a large part of Web3 infrastructure. It was, not long ago, one of the latest projects to put out a call for assistance as financial resources ran thin.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Ethereum’s public goods landscape (in the sense of “teams building and open-sourcing things that are maximally valuable to our ecosystem”) has no shortage of talent: the ecosystem is full of professionals doing work that is deeply technical, widely relied upon, and chronically under-incentivized.
These are the projects that quietly keep the ecosystem secure, reliable, and capable of evolving.
They also tend to share a vulnerability: while they are strong at research and engineering, they often lack the fundraising, operational, and business capacity needed to remain future-proof.
The basic symptom is: everyone depends on shared infrastructure, but no one wants to risk ending up at a competitive disadvantage by being the one to fund it.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: Ad-hoc funding is fragile, political, and cyclical.
Reliability of funding flows is almost as important as the funding itself.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official Ethereum Foundation - Project Odin portal at https://blog.ethereum.org/2026/02/27/project-odin. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

description: From the experimental first round that distributed 200,000 FIL to 99 projects, to the refined second round that allocated 300,000 FIL across 97 projects, the Filecoin community has consistently demonstrated that public goods funding drives real innovation.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: RetroPGF is an upgrade to Filecoin’s core economic mechanisms that addresses a gap in funding for public goods.
It sets out to fund contributions that have generated recognized impact for Filecoin using Optimism-style retroactive public goods funding.
In essence, funding in recognition rather than anticipation.
Today, the RetroPGF team is thrilled to announce the launch of FIL RetroPGF Round 3.

sections.heading: Program details

Applications will open in late September with voting and allocation, via the Drips platform, following in October and November.

description: For the moment, funding requests are being reviewed through ProPGF, the Filecoin network’s public goods funding program, which is funded in part by Filecoin Foundation. Upcoming ProPGF programs, dates and criteria are posted atfilpgf.io/propgf.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Filecoin Foundation routes much of its public-goods funding through ProPGF, the network’s community funding process. Builders submit proposals for storage tooling, media archives, and infrastructure that grows verifiable storage markets.
Upcoming ProPGF rounds, deadlines, and scopes are announced on fil.org and community forums rather than a single static intake.
Grantees are encouraged to publish retrieval benchmarks and storage deal metrics so the community can verify impact between payout milestones.

Current RFPs cover FEVM security testing, a programmable PoRep proving pipeline, UCAN delegation for wallets and AI agents, SRA service orchestrators, quantum readiness, and stewardship of the docs and Kernel functions.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: R&D backs work that closes gaps in the network before they become problems.
RFPs are published as gaps are identified and applications are reviewed as they arrive, with funding released in stages as the work proves out.
The strongest proposals name the gap they close and say why it matters now.
R&D funds work aimed at a specific gap in the network: something missing, thinly covered, or dependent on a single implementation.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: The strongest proposals name that gap plainly and explain why closing it matters now rather than later.
Most of this work sits alongside the pods, supporting what they're building without duplicating what they already own.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: ✓ Work that closes a named gap in the network
✓ Where relevant, the Kernel function or Revenue Development roadmap it would strengthen
✓ Work that sits alongside the pods, supporting them without duplicating what they own
✓ A second implementation where the network currently depends on just one
✓ Findings the ecosystem can use even if the work itself does not continue
✓ A credible route from this stage into ongoing Kernel or Revenue Development funding
✕ Work with no credible path to shipping inside the grant horizon
✕ Marketing campaigns, business development, acquisitions, and one-off incentives

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: R&D is request-driven. the usual way in is a response to a published RFP rather than an unsolicited proposal.

name: Galaxy Bitcoin Quantum Readiness Initiative
description: The initiative has three pillars: → Up to $5M in developer grants for post-quantum solutions → Ongoing research & publishing via Galaxy Research → A Quantum Advisory Council of leading experts

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Commits up to $5 million in developer grants; establishes Quantum Advisory Council; calls on industry to join the effort
Galaxy today announced the launch of the Galaxy Bitcoin Quantum Readiness Initiative, a multi-pillar program dedicated to preparing Bitcoin for the threat posed by advances in quantum computing.

The initiative includes up to $5 million in grant funding for developers working on post-quantum solutions for Bitcoin, a dedicated research and publishing program through Galaxy Research, and the formation of a Quantum Advisory Council of leading experts in quantum computing and post-quantum cryptography.
Bitcoin's security relies on elliptic curve cryptography, which could be broken by a sufficiently powerful quantum computer.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: While no cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists today, the expected timeline for one to be built is compressing.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalized its first post-quantum cryptography standards in 2024, and a recent executive order set a 2031 deadline for the federal government to defend against quantum attacks on classical cryptography.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official Galaxy Bitcoin Quantum Readiness Initiative portal at https://www.galaxy.com/newsroom/galaxy-launches-bitcoin-quantum-readiness-initiative. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs: What is the difference between the Startup Program and the Partner Program? The Startup Program gives eligible companies a direct 50% discount on up to 10 IDE or All Products Pack subscriptions plus up to 10 team or learning tools over five years. The Partner Program is for incubators, accelerators, and VCs that receive six months of free licenses before switching their portfolio companies to the standard startup discount.
How long does application review take? Startup applications are reviewed within about 48 hours. Partner applications are reviewed within about seven days.
Can we receive the startup discount more than once? No. Each eligible organization may receive the Startup Program discount only once, and it cannot be extended to subsidiaries.
When does the discount expire? Five years after approval or once you reach the license caps (10 IDE/APP and 10 team or learning subscriptions).

Do we need to reapply for additional licenses? No. Approved startups can purchase more eligible licenses through the store and the discount applies automatically at checkout, within the published caps.
Can the discount apply to floating or team-wide IDE licenses? No. IDE licenses are per user and the startup discount does not cover floating license models.
Can we combine the startup discount with other JetBrains promotions? No. The Startup Program discount cannot be stacked with other offers.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official Merge Grants portal at https://sologrants.com/guide/solo-grant. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

name: MetaGammaDelta Grants
description: MetaGammaDelta Grants provide micro-funding, mentorship, and community backing for women-led Web3 projects, DAO tooling, and decentralized public goods.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: MetaGammaDelta is an inclusive, women-led DAO focused on supporting female and non-binary founders in Web3. The DAO distributes micro-grants to empower early-stage builders turning ideas into live prototypes.
Alongside capital, grantees receive hands-on mentoring from experienced Web3 operators, technical code reviews, community beta testing, and introductions to leading venture capital funds.

sections.heading: What reviewers look for
bullets: Projects led or co-founded by women or non-binary entrepreneurs across all sectors of Web3 and digital sovereignty.
Working prototypes, open-source code repositories, or clear MVP roadmaps ready for execution.
Collaborative community initiatives, educational programs, and public goods that expand diversity in tech.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit an application via the MetaGammaDelta portal. The DAO membership conducts community reviews, interviews founders, and votes on grant allocations during periodic funding cycles.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

The zkApp trackis for zero-knowledge applications, written using SnarkyJS and deployed on Mina Protocol.
User personas will vary, and won’t just be developer-focused.
The Dev Tooling track is aimed at funding ‘start-ups for start-ups’.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: The end users of these applications or services will be developers who are building zkApps and need these primitives to build successfully.

name: Mintlify Startups
description: Mintlify for Startups awards qualified developer-first teams with six months of free Mintlify Pro, providing modern MDX documentation hosting, API reference sync, and interactive playgrounds.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Mintlify enables developer tools, SDKs, and web3 protocols to build beautiful, conversion-focused documentation out of the box. Mintlify syncs directly with GitHub repositories using standard MDX files.
The startup grant provides six months of Mintlify Pro, unlocking custom domain hosting, OpenAPI and Swagger interactive endpoint testers, built-in AI search assistants, and user engagement analytics.

sections.heading: Documentation capabilities
bullets: Git-backed documentation where doc changes are reviewed and merged via standard GitHub pull requests.
Interactive API explorer allowing developers to test HTTP and RPC requests directly from documentation pages.
Built-in AI-powered search that answers developer questions accurately using indexed documentation pages.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Fill out the brief startup form on Mintlify’s website with your company domain and GitHub repo link. Upon qualification, the Mintlify team applies the six-month Pro credit to your organization.
Submissions are verified directly against partner registry databases. Once approved, credit codes and tier upgrades are provisioned directly to your company administrative account.

name: Miro for Startups
description: Miro for Startups awards early-stage teams up to $1,000 in workspace credits to collaborate on visual system architecture diagrams, user journey mapping, and product sprint roadmaps.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Miro provides a collaborative visual workspace that empowers distributed founding teams to brainstorm, map complex software architectures, and run agile planning sessions on an infinite canvas.
The Miro Startup Program provides up to $1,000 in software credits valid for Team or Business plans, unlocking unlimited boards, advanced diagramming shapes (UML, AWS, Kubernetes), and video chat.

sections.heading: Collaboration benefits
bullets: Extensive technical diagramming libraries including AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, and Cisco networking shapes.
Real-time collaborative whiteboarding with voting, timers, private mode, and breakout working areas.
Integrations with Jira, Confluence, Slack, and Figma to synchronize visual designs with engineering backlogs.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply through the Miro for Startups page using your company domain and accelerator or venture partner code. Once verified, credits are deposited directly into your Miro workspace billing account.
Submissions are verified directly against partner registry databases. Once approved, credit codes and tier upgrades are provisioned directly to your company administrative account.

name: Modal Startup Program
description: The Modal Startup Program awards high-performance GPU and CPU cloud credits to early-stage teams building serverless AI inference, model fine-tuning, and heavy compute pipelines.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Modal enables developers to run Python code in the cloud with instant container spin-up, zero server management, and automated scaling from zero to thousands of GPUs. The startup program provides credits to offset heavy computational experimentation.

Teams use Modal for real-time model serving (vLLM, Diffusers), asynchronous distributed batch tasks, voice transcription pipelines, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning on modern NVIDIA H100, A100, and L4 GPUs.

sections.heading: What developers receive
bullets: Generous monthly compute credits covering high-end NVIDIA GPU compute hours and serverless CPU jobs.
Instant cold starts under one second for custom containerized environments written in pure Python.
Direct engineering support in a dedicated Slack channel with Modal runtime and infrastructure engineers.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Register for a Modal account and submit the startup credit request form describing your workload requirements, current GPU infrastructure, and company roadmap. Applications are evaluated within two business days.
Applications undergo rolling review with technical verification. Approved founders gain access to the dedicated startup community and regular solution architecture office hours.

name: Morph Payment Accelerator
description: The Morph Payment Accelerator provides funding, technical mentoring, and consumer distribution support for teams building payment apps and consumer rollups on Morph Layer 2.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Morph is a consumer-focused Ethereum Layer 2 utilizing a decentralized sequencer network and optimistic zkEVM rollups to power seamless retail transactions and daily consumer decentralized apps.
The Payment Accelerator program incubates founders creating user-friendly mobile payment rails, merchant checkout integrations, social tipping bots, and localized fiat-to-crypto ramps on Morph.

sections.heading: Focus areas
bullets: Mobile payment interfaces with gas abstraction, social logins, and instant confirmation for peer-to-peer transfers.
Merchant payment SDKs that enable online stores and physical retailers to settle stablecoins with sub-cent transaction costs.
Consumer loyalty programs, reward points tokenization, and recurring subscription payment protocols.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply on the Morph accelerator portal with your product demo, pitch deck, target user geography, and technical integration architecture. Accepted teams join a multi-week intensive acceleration cohort.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Movemaker Grant Program
description: The Movemaker Grant Program awards developer grants, code audits, and incubation to builders launching applications written in the Move language across Aptos, Sui, and Movement networks.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Move programming language offers unmatched safety, asset-oriented programming, and formal verification capabilities. The Movemaker Grant Program accelerates the global Move builder ecosystem.

The program distributes milestone funding and technical mentorship to developers building Move smart contracts, cross-Move liquidity bridges, developer frameworks, and security auditing tools across Move chains.

sections.heading: Priority development categories
bullets: Native Move DeFi protocols, automated market makers, and liquid restaking derivatives built on Move chains.
Cross-chain bridges and interoperability modules facilitating asset movement between Move networks and the EVM.
Developer tooling including Move testing frameworks, static analysis linters, and educational tutorials.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your proposal through the Movemaker website. Provide your GitHub repository, team backgrounds, Move smart contract architecture, and a staged milestone delivery schedule.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Mozilla Foundation Awards & Fellowships
description: The Mozilla Foundation Awards & Fellowships program provides funding between $10,000 and $100,000+ for researchers, open-source developers, and civil society leaders building a healthier internet.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Mozilla’s grantmaking and fellowship initiatives champion open-source tools, algorithmic transparency, trustworthy artificial intelligence, and digital privacy. The foundation supports individuals and small teams creating public interest technologies.

Awardees receive flexible grant capital, collaborative residency cohorts, international research visibility, and technical collaboration opportunities with Mozilla engineers and policy experts worldwide.

sections.heading: Core thematic priorities
bullets: Trustworthy AI systems that prioritize user agency, transparent training data, and algorithmic accountability.
Open web standards, decentralized identity frameworks, and zero-knowledge privacy technologies.
Digital safety and defense tools that protect journalists, researchers, and vulnerable communities online.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Review open award cycles on the Mozilla Foundation website. Submit an initial statement of purpose detailing your project’s technical roadmap, open-source licensing, and community impact. Shortlisted applicants participate in video panel interviews.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub
description: Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub provides software startups with up to $150,000 in Azure cloud credits, OpenAI API access, GitHub Enterprise licenses, and technical advisory support.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Founders Hub is an open-access platform designed for entrepreneurs at every stage of growth, from initial ideation to scale. Startups do not need venture capital backing or institutional affiliation to qualify for initial benefits.

As companies build and hit milestones, credit allocations scale up to $150,000 in Microsoft Azure computing, Azure OpenAI Service access with GPT-4 and embeddings, Microsoft 365 productivity suites, and LinkedIn tooling.

sections.heading: Key perks across tiers
bullets: Tiered Azure credits that unlock progressively based on prototype progress, customer traction, and usage.
Direct access to Azure OpenAI Service endpoints with enterprise data privacy guarantees and dedicated rate limits.
Complimentary 1-on-1 technical advisory sessions with Microsoft cloud solution architects and AI engineers.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Sign in with a LinkedIn or Microsoft account on the Founders Hub portal. Complete a brief profile describing your business model and product vision. Approvals are generally issued within minutes for entry-tier benefits.

name: MultiversX Grants
description: MultiversX Grants award milestone-based funding, technical support, and ecosystem marketing to developers deploying high-throughput dApps on MultiversX sovereign state shards.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: MultiversX (formerly Elrond) is a high-speed, carbon-negative blockchain network utilizing Adaptive State Sharding and a Secure Proof of Stake consensus to process over 15,000 transactions per second.

The MultiversX Grants Program funds developers building on its Rust-based smart contract environment, supporting teams across decentralized finance, digital identity, web3 gaming, and mobile consumer apps.

sections.heading: Focus areas & qualifications
bullets: Rust smart contracts demonstrating clean architecture, unit test coverage, and efficient execution on the MultiversX VM.
Integrations with xPortal (the flagship consumer mobile wallet with millions of active users).
Enterprise digital asset tokenization, decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN), and real-world asset workflows.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit an application via the MultiversX ecosystem portal. Provide an overview of your team, smart contract architecture in Rust, live demo or GitHub links, and a milestone-based budget schedule.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Get sponsorship for the open source you maintain
Developers build on open source that a small number of maintainers keep running.
Neon commits a minimum of $200,000 a year to sponsoring those maintainers in cash.
Each sponsored project receives a monthly amount from that pool through GitHub Sponsors.

sections.heading: Program details

Your project doesn't need to use Neon or Postgres to apply.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Monthly cash sponsorshipNeon sponsors your project through GitHub Sponsors with a fixed monthly amount for a six-month term, paid from its annual sponsorship pool. You set up payouts and tax details in your GitHub Sponsors profile.
Renewable termsNear the end of each six-month term, we review the sponsorship with you and decide whether to renew it. Sponsorships don't renew automatically.

Neon and AI Gateway creditsProjects we support can also receive up to $5,000 in Neon credits and up to $5,000 in Neon AI Gateway credits, if they want them. The credits are optional and don't affect the cash sponsorship.

A relationship if you want oneWe're happy to work with maintainers on content, events, integrations, or product feedback when it makes sense for both sides. None of it is a condition of the sponsorship.
Show the Neon logo with a link in one agreed place: your README, your project homepage, your documentation site, or a sponsors page.
Label it as a sponsorship, for example "Sponsored by Neon."
Keep the placement live for the full term, and tell us if it moves or if the project's ownership changes.

name: Nosana AI Grants
description: Nosana AI Grants award $5,000 to $50,000 in cash and decentralized GPU compute credits to developers building open-source AI inference pipelines and agents on Solana.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Nosana is the decentralized GPU grid built on Solana, connecting consumers with cost-effective, crowd-sourced GPU hardware for AI model inference, embeddings generation, and fine-tuning.

The Nosana AI Grants Program provides developers with capital and compute hours to build and deploy open-source LLMs, conversational agents, image generators, and automated workflows on Nosana’s GPU network.

sections.heading: Eligible AI applications
bullets: AI-powered decentralized agents that execute automated onchain transactions, trading, or data analytics on Solana.
Open-source AI developer tooling, model deployment SDKs, and container orchestration pipelines using Nosana nodes.
Consumer consumer AI web apps utilizing Nosana’s inference endpoints for low-cost, high-speed model generation.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply via the Nosana grants portal. Detail your target AI models, expected monthly GPU compute consumption, GitHub repository, and planned Solana mainnet deployment milestones.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Notion for Startups
description: Notion for Startups offers discounted Business workspace access with Notion AI for qualifying young companies referred through partner investors or accelerators.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Eligible startups can receive up to six months of Business plan access with Notion AI for teams under roughly 100 employees, with partner-specific tiers offering shorter trials.
The perk is designed for internal knowledge bases, product specs, and fundraising rooms rather than customer-facing wikis alone.
Partner referrals usually unlock the longest trial window, so confirm your investor’s offer code before creating a paid workspace.

sections.heading: Eligibility and benefits
bullets: Company must meet Notion’s published age, funding, and partner referral requirements.
Benefits include collaborative docs, databases, AI-assisted writing, and standard startup onboarding templates.
Renewal or conversion to paid plans follows Notion’s published startup terms after the promotional window.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply through your accelerator or VC partner link listed on notion.com/startups. If you lack a partner code, review the page for alternate eligibility paths and required company verification documents.

name: OrangeDAO Grants
description: OrangeDAO Grants provide venture funding, mentorship, and community backing from a collective of over 1,000 Y Combinator alumni investing in early-stage Web3 and AI founders.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: OrangeDAO is the premier decentralized organization of Y Combinator alumni founders. The DAO supports high-potential entrepreneurs building foundational protocols, developer infrastructure, and consumer applications.
