name: Open Technology Fund (OTF) – Internet Freedom Fund
description: Provides non-dilutive grant funding for open source tools, circumvention tech, secure communications, and censorship resistance research worldwide.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: This fund supports innovative internet freedom projects, including technology development, research, digital security projects, and convenings.
The Internet Freedom Fund is the primary opportunity through which Open Technology Fund supports innovative global internet freedom projects.
These projects are focused on technology development and implementation, but can also include applied research, convenings, and digital security projects.
See below for more details about each category.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: OTF prioritizes projects coming from individuals or organizations who are applying for the first time, identify as under-represented within the field, and address areas that are underfunded.
Applications to the Fund go through a two-stage application process and are accepted on a rolling basis.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Taking an existing open-source internet freedom technology and improving upon its security, usability, and adaptability
Developing content redistribution methods to aid in content access behind government firewalls
Improving security standards, quality assurance, and best practices within core infrastructure projects
Research that focuses on real-time monitoring and analysis of threats to internet freedom
Research exploring new methods or improvements of censorship circumvention tools
Efforts that increase the understanding and awareness of the Internet freedom community, their roles, and how they contribute to maintaining a free and open internet

User research identifying the needs of people living under repressive surveillance and censorship, how technologies and tools can address those needs, and how these tools can introduce usability and localization improvements
Targeted research and development gatherings designed to improve collaboration and knowledge sharing between projects in the areas of privacy, circumvention technology, and digital security

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Successful applicants are paired with an OTF program manager who will oversee all project monitoring and evaluation for the duration of the contract. Monitoring and evaluation assessments are based on predetermined and agreed-upon metrics, deliverables, and goals as laid out by the applicant in the project proposal.
Stage 1: Submit a Concept Note through OTF’s online application system in which you tell us about your project idea through a short form.

name: Polymesh Network Grants
description: Receive funding to build open-source features and functionality on top of Polymesh

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: At the Polymesh Association, we want to improve and extend the Polymesh ecosystem.
We offer a Grants Program to award grants to our community developers for building and extending Polymesh features.
In this repo, you'll find how to apply for a grant using our Grants Program.
For more information about Polymesh, visit our website.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: Anyone is welcome to apply for a grant.
Projects funded through our programs are broad in scope, but our focus lies on strong technical projects that add value to the Polymesh ecosystem.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Process 1. Application 2. Application Review 3. Milestone Delivery and Payment Changes to a Grant after Approval
It presents a well-researched or tested concept, for which ideally you are able to show some prior work.

You can demonstrate that the project will be maintained after completion of the grant, be it through an obvious commitment to the technology from your side, additional funding sources or an existing business model.
Your application is rich in technical details and well-defined.
You can clearly present how your project stands out among competitors or implements technology that doesn't exist in the ecosystem yet.

All code produced as part of a grant must be open-sourced, and it must also not rely on closed-source software for full functionality. We prefer Apache 2.0, but GPLv3, MIT or Unlicense are also acceptable.
We do not award grants for projects that have been the object of a successful token sale.
As a general rule, teams are asked to finish a grant before applying for another one.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your proposal through the official Polymesh Network Grants application portal at https://github.com/PolymeshAssociation/Grants-Program. Detail your technical architecture, open-source repository, and milestone roadmap.

Marketing, education, and referral programs that expand awareness responsibly.
Committees, sub-DAOs, and working groups that serve the PoolTogether ecosystem.
Security reviews and code audits for integrations touching user funds.

sections.heading: Program details

The grant program will run across the full year of 2026 and consists of:

SafePal Officially Integrates Arc Mainnet with Native USDC and EURC Vaults

Unauthorized Access To A Subset Of Customer Order Information

Projects and builders still need cost-efficient, high-impact growth tools that deliver meaningful and relevant results. This section of the grant will offer resources to boost user retention and brand image, such as premium listings in the SafePal Dapp center and homepage, the opportunity to collaborate and create in-depth customized tasks to drive actual product usage and track conversions, filtering relevant users by whitelisting based on asset and behavior to combat bot farmers and more. name: Scaleup Europe Fund
description: The European Commission has completed the final legal steps required to establish the Scaleup Europe Fund, a major new investment initiative designed to help Europe’s most promising technology companies grow into global market leaders. With a target size of €5 billion, the Fund will invest directly in European scaleups operating in strategic technology sectors. Its first investments are expected to take place in the coming weeks.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Scaleup Europe Fund is a new, multi-billion late-stage and growth fund aimed at investing in the most promising European companies in strategic tech areas, such as artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, semiconductor technologies, robotics and autonomous systems, energy technologies, space technologies, biotechnologies, medical technologies, advanced materials, and agritech, and across all parts of Europe.
The Scaleup Europe Fund responds to the urgent need for Europe to boost investments in scaleups and close the gap with global leaders.
The new Scaleup Europe Fund brings new momentum to Europe’s scaleup ecosystem, anchored in public-private cooperation.

Alongside the Commission, the group of founding investors in the Fund include Novo Holdings, EIFO (Export and Investment Fund of Denmark), CriteriaCaixa, Santander/Mouro Capital, Fondazione Compagnia San Paolo/ Intesa Sanpaolo/Fondazione Cariplo, APG Asset Management, acting on behalf of Dutch pension fund ABP, Wallenberg Investments and Allianz.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: The Fund will be part of the existing EIC Fund umbrella structure but with a fully privately owned and market-based fund manager.

The fund is a key initiative of the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy, announced by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in her 2025 State of the Union Address, aimed at making major investments in fast-growing companies in strategic tech areas, so that "the best of Europe can choose Europe".

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit your application through the official Scaleup Europe Fund portal at https://eic.ec.europa.eu/eic-fund/scaleup-europe-fund_en. Include project architecture, technical milestones, team backgrounds, and testnet deployment timelines.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Snowflake for Startups enables founders to build data-intensive applications, predictive AI pipelines, and native multi-tenant SaaS products on the Snowflake Data Cloud without managing data warehouse infrastructure.

Selected startups receive introductory compute credits to deploy scalable virtual warehouses, secure data sharing feeds, and interactive Streamlit analytics apps directly on top of their cloud data lake.

sections.heading: Key benefits
bullets: Snowflake platform credits to subsidize warehousing, data ingestion, and analytical SQL compute.
Architectural guidance on data modeling, cost optimization, and secure multi-tenant SaaS partitioning.
Opportunities to publish monetized datasets and native applications to the global Snowflake Data Marketplace.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Fill out the startup application form on Snowflake’s official website with your funding stage, company domain, and primary cloud provider. An account executive contacts eligible founders to activate benefits.
Applications undergo rolling review with technical verification. Approved founders gain access to the dedicated startup community and regular solution architecture office hours.

name: Snyk for Startups
description: Snyk for Startups provides young software teams with discounted developer security licenses, automated vulnerability scanning for open-source dependencies, code security, and container images.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Snyk enables developers to find and fix security vulnerabilities directly in their IDEs, pull requests, and CI/CD pipelines. The startup program gives early teams enterprise security capabilities at startup pricing.

Engineering teams automatically scan open-source npm, pip, and cargo packages for known CVEs, detect code security flaws in proprietary repositories, and monitor container configurations before production deploy.

sections.heading: Security tooling features
bullets: Automated pull request checks that identify security vulnerabilities and suggest one-click dependency upgrades.
Snyk Code static application security testing (SAST) with real-time feedback directly inside VS Code and JetBrains.
Container and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, Kubernetes) configuration scanning for compliance gaps.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Sign up on the Snyk for Startups portal. Submit your venture capital or accelerator partner details to receive custom startup pricing and unlock extended security testing limits.
Submissions are verified directly against partner registry databases. Once approved, credit codes and tier upgrades are provisioned directly to your company administrative account.

name: Solana Foundation Grants & Funding
description: The Solana Foundation Funding Program aims to connect builders, creators, and founders to the best source of funding for their work. This may be through the Solana Foundation or other ecosystem sources.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: In the Solana ecosystem’s open-source spirit, the Solana Foundation supports projects that generate public goods for the community and give other ecosystem participants the opportunity to learn from and build on your work.
The Solana Foundation primarily provides funding in the following ways:
the following are a set of guidelines for the Solana Foundation funding application only.
Ecosystem sources of funding may have different processes.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: All funding applicants for Solana Foundation standard and convertible grants are required to fill out the application here.
All applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Milestone-based convertible grants for public goods with a commercial component
Requests for Proposals (RFPs) for specific ideas the Foundation is looking to fund
Clarify how your project provides a public good for the Solana network
Lay out a well structured budget proposal, and include thoughtful milestones

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Applicants will be notified via the email provided in their application whether their proposal has been accepted or not.

name: Solana Mobile Builder Grants
description: Supporting developers building mobile-first crypto applications with funding, resources, and ecosystem access to expand what's possible on Solana.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Solana Mobile Builder Grants fund teams shipping mobile-first crypto experiences on Saga, Seed Vault, and the Solana Mobile Stack.
Reviewers score proposals on mobile UX quality, Solana Mobile Stack integration depth, and realistic milestone timelines.
Grantees are expected to demo builds on physical Saga hardware or compliant emulators before each payout tranche.

sections.heading: Evaluation criteria
bullets: Mobile-first implementation with clear use of Seed Vault or Mobile Wallet Adapter.
Open-source or community components that other builders can reuse.
Milestones tied to testnet or device demos with defined user or transaction targets.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Use the Solana Mobile grants page to submit scope, team background, and funding use of funds. Include APK or TestFlight links when available so reviewers can evaluate the current build.
Describe Seed Vault or Mobile Wallet Adapter usage in your architecture diagram so reviewers can verify stack compliance quickly.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Solana Scholars
description: The Solana Scholars program awards student developer grants, collegiate hackathon prizes, and research fellowships to university students building open-source protocols on Solana.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Solana Scholars is an educational grant initiative sponsored by the Solana Foundation, designed to empower collegiate developers, researchers, and university blockchain clubs around the world.
The program awards project development stipends, conference travel sponsorships, technical mentoring from core Solana engineers, and incubator access for student-founded Web3 startups.

sections.heading: Student opportunities
bullets: Milestone-based project grants for student-led software development, open-source SDKs, and research papers on Solana.
Travel stipends and tickets to participate in Solana Hacker Houses and the annual Solana Breakpoint conference.
Fast-tracked entry into leading Web3 startup accelerators and direct introductions to top venture capital investors.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Complete the application form on the Solana Scholars portal with proof of current academic enrollment, your GitHub profile, and a description of your proposed open-source Solana project.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Sovereign Tech Fund (STF)
provider: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs
description: The Sovereign Tech Fund (STF) provides €50,000 to €500,000+ in non-dilutive open-source funding to maintain and fortify critical digital infrastructure, open protocols, and security libraries.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action, the Sovereign Tech Fund invests in foundational open-source technologies that underpin global digital ecosystems, internet routing, operating systems, and cryptography.

STF awards sustainable, milestone-driven funding to maintainers and core developers to pay for security audits, automated testing infrastructure, bug fixes, performance refactoring, and community governance.

sections.heading: Eligible open-source projects
bullets: Core libraries, programming language compilers, cryptographic primitives, and foundational developer utilities.
Critical internet protocols, time-synchronization tools, and foundational operating system components.
Open-source technologies that demonstrate widespread global dependency, active maintenance, and open governance.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit an application through the Sovereign Tech Fund website during active submission rounds. Outline your project’s dependency graph, current maintenance bottlenecks, and planned security deliverables. Contracts are issued as public funding agreements.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Spiral Grants
description: Spiral provides grants to projects and individual contributors around the world to help achieve our mission of making sure that money and intelligence become lasting, open source public goods.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: We cast a wide net for non-commercial projects that will have significant long-term impact on either the open source AI ecosystem or bitcoin—maybe even both.
If you have a big idea in mind, go ahead and Apply Now by sending us a detailed proposal.
If you're looking for inspiration, here are some areas of work that we think are, and will continue to be, important:
Spiral is especially interested in funding projects that make open source AI:

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: How can open models—and the related tooling, agents and apps in the open ecosystem—win over closed alternatives?

We’d love to see open local models be more efficient, more private, more powerful for specific uses (like scientific research) and more broadly accessible, especially in constrained environments like mobile and embedded hardware.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: To apply for a grant, send a detailed proposal—with a focus on the scale and longevity of impact of your project and its unique contribution—to grants@spiral.xyz. Or just smash the button.

name: SSOJet Startup Program
description: SSOJet’s startup offer provides 50% off enterprise single sign-on for twelve months to qualifying young companies that need SAML and OIDC without building auth infrastructure in-house.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The program targets startups that must pass enterprise security reviews but cannot yet afford full IdP contracts. SSOJet hosts the integration while your team focuses on core product delivery.
Non-profit applicants use the same form and may qualify when they meet published eligibility criteria for discounted enterprise auth.

sections.heading: How to apply
bullets: Complete the startup application with company details and expected monthly active SSO users.
SSOJet reviews within roughly one to two business days and emails onboarding instructions.
Approved teams configure SAML or OIDC connections using SSOJet’s guided setup wizard.

sections.heading: After approval
paragraphs: Monitor seat usage during the promotional year and plan migration to standard pricing before renewal if you outgrow startup limits.
Document SAML attribute mappings and SCIM settings if enterprise customers require them during security questionnaires.
Keep an admin contact on file for certificate expiry notices so production logins do not break silently.

name: Stacks grants program
description: The Stacks Grants Program provides non-dilutive milestone funding to developers building smart contracts, Bitcoin DeFi (sBTC), and decentralized apps secured by Bitcoin proof-of-transfer.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Stacks brings smart contracts and decentralized applications directly to Bitcoin, utilizing its novel Proof of Transfer (PoX) consensus and sBTC for 1:1 non-custodial Bitcoin settlement.
The Stacks Grants Program funds community developers, researchers, and entrepreneurs who expand Bitcoin programmability across DeFi, digital artifacts, developer tooling, and decentralized identity.

sections.heading: Key focus areas
bullets: sBTC financial primitives: Lending, decentralized trading, and automated yield protocols collateralized natively by Bitcoin.
Clarity smart contracts: Highly predictable, decidable smart contracts that eliminate entire classes of exploits.
Developer tooling, indexers, Hiro SDK integrations, and educational resources for the Stacks ecosystem.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit a formal grant proposal on the Stacks Foundation GitHub grants repository. Define measurable milestones, deliverables, and budget in STX or USD. Community review and voting guide final funding decisions.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: Stacks Foundation Grants
description: The Stacks Foundation funds builders advancing a Bitcoin-secured Web3 through the Stacks Endowment, community DeGrants, and coordinated security bounties across core ecosystem teams.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Stacks Foundation grant programs back open internet infrastructure on Stacks, with a focus on builders, researchers, and community organizers advancing Bitcoin-secured applications.
Funding options include Stacks Endowment Grants for staged project work and DeGrants, a community-led process where members direct smaller awards to ideas they want to see shipped.

sections.heading: Stacks Endowment Grants
paragraphs: The endowment publishes tracks for teams getting started, builders shipping products, and community programs that grow adoption. Active awards and milestones are listed on the Stacks Endowment site.
Applicants should tie each milestone to measurable on-chain or open-source deliverables reviewers can verify publicly.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Several ecosystem teams run Immunefi programs for responsible disclosure. Payout ranges vary by project severity tables and are separate from standard grants.
bullets: Hiro and Leather run security bounty programs for their wallets and developer tooling.
BitFlow, Zest, Granite, and StackingDao host Immunefi bounties with disclosed maximum awards.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

name: Stanford Blockchain Accelerator
description: The Stanford Blockchain Accelerator provides equity-free incubation, mentorship, and investor access to early-stage founders building groundbreaking blockchain protocols and applications.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Run by the Stanford Blockchain Club, the Stanford Blockchain Accelerator is one of the most successful non-profit, student-led Web3 incubators in the world, having supported dozens of top venture-backed startups.

Selected founders participate in an intensive multi-week curriculum, receiving direct guidance from leading industry founders, academic cryptographers, legal experts, and top-tier venture capitalists.

sections.heading: Accelerator highlights
bullets: Completely non-dilutive, zero-equity incubation curriculum tailored for early-stage crypto founders.
Weekly masterclasses and private office hours with Tier 1 Web3 founders, protocol architects, and VCs.
Exclusive Demo Day in Silicon Valley attended by over 100 institutional blockchain investment funds.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply through the Stanford Blockchain Accelerator website during open cohort application windows. Submit your pitch deck, product demo, and team bios. Stanford affiliation is not mandatory for consideration.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: StarkWare
description: StarkWare is excited to announce the launch of a $4 million venture fund to foster the growth of blockchain startups in Africa. The fund is a testament to StarkWare’s belief in the potential of blockchain in Africa, a continent historically underserved by traditional institutions, to drive global crypto adoption.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Africa-focused venture fund is spearheaded by Kheireddine Kamal, a seasoned African entrepreneur and investor.
Kamal brings deep experience in business development, blockchain, and seed investments to the initiative, having worked with several startups across the continent.

The Africa investment team will focus on early-stage teams, particularly those at the pre-seed and seed stages, with an emphasis on projects aiming to deploy their solutions on Starknet, the zero-knowledge (ZK) rollup massively scaling Ethereum.
Early-stage startups can apply for grants of up to $150,000, with larger investments available to more advanced teams (generally up to $500,000).

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: Grants are designed to help projects at different stages of development.
StarkWare is particularly interested in teams that combine technical expertise with business acumen, and are looking to deploy their blockchain projects on Starknet.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Early-stage startups can apply for grants of up to $150,000, with larger investments available to more advanced teams (generally up to $500,000). Grants are designed to help projects at different stages of development. StarkWare is particularly interested in teams that combine technical expertise with business acumen, and are looking to deploy their blockchain projects on Starknet.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: We process millions of signals monthly, incorporating the latest and most up-to-date information spanning compliance, regulatory data, potential threats, and community-sourced insights.
What does this mean for your integration?

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Get up to $10,000 in DD.xyz API credits to add an extra layer of due diligence to your dApp Integrate Webacy's robust APIs to equip you and your users with the critical intelligence needed for effective due diligence and decentralized decision-making within the web3 ecosystem. Empower them with the tools to navigate the landscape confidently and make informed choices. Webacy's Risk Engine is at the core of all out API endpoints. This powerful engine provides the broadest coverage across the blockchain ecosystem by aggregating data from over 15 diverse data providers, complemented by our proprietary data analytics and advanced algorithms. We process millions of signals monthly, incorporating the latest and most up-to-date information spanning compliance, regulatory data, potential threats, and community-sourced insights. What does this mean for your integration? By utilizing DD.xys’ APIs, you provide your users with access to the most extensive and current risk-related data available. Unlike solutions relying on a single data source, our multi-provider approach offers a comprehensive and nuanced understanding of the complexities within web3. Our engine combines the power of AI-driven analysis with human refinement, ensuring both efficient processing and highly accurate information for user evaluation. Facilitating informed decision-making requires providing relevant data across the web3 journey. Our APIs deliver crucial insights at key interaction points: Wallet Risk Insights: Enable users to understand the risk profiles associated with different wallets and their activities. Transaction Intelligence: Provide users with data to evaluate the potential risks associated with specific transactions. Token Analysis: Equip users with comprehensive data and risk assessments for all tokens Smart Contract Analysis: Offer users information to assess the security and potential risks of interacting with various smart contracts. Contextual Awareness: Equip users with the information needed to understand the broader context surrounding their web3 interactions. The DD.xyz Platform is architected to empower projects and end-users throughout their web3 experience. Our APIs are designed to be valuable at every stage, providing the data necessary for individuals to conduct their own due diligence and make well-informed decisions. Built by a team with deep expertise in crypto, cybersecurity, AI, and data integration, Webacy provides the foundational data layer for informed participation in web3. We process vast amounts of information, allowing your users to access critical intelligence and exercise greater autonomy in their web3 journey. Integrate our infrastructure and empower your users with the knowledge they need to navigate web3 with confidence. ️ Apply for the grant now. We are receiving a large volume of applications, and may not have the time to give detailed feedback on every submission. Please keep that in mind before you apply. 🏻‍ Our APIs Threat Risks API This API discovers the risk of any on-chain address. This includes any contract, wallet, EOA (Externally Owned Account), token, NFT, or otherwise. It analyzes an address' threat to others. It returns risk data associated with the supplied address. It flags if the address appears in any sanctioned databases or has been historically flagged as malicious. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Filtering addresses for spam/sybil Blocking high-risk addresses from utilizing your service (compliance, platform safety) Flagging high-risk addresses (tokens, contracts, P2P participants) Example implementation: Block, limit and/or track unwanted addresses (like spam, bots, clones, OFAC/SCAM/Blacklisted/Terrorism financing addresses) from entering/signing in to your platform. Highlighting token risk analysis prior to a swap, or within a users wallet. Approval Risks API This API analyzes the risks associated with token approvals given by a specific address. It returns data indicating potentially risky approvals, such as those granting unlimited allowance to suspicious contracts. This helps users understand and manage their token permissions. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Alerting users about potentially dangerous token approvals Providing insights into a user's approval history Identifying and mitigating risks related to token drain attacks Example implementation: Display historical risk data to a user. Better understand a user’s behavioral patterns. Provide recommendations to users based on transactional health history. Assess a user’s historical activity in order to approve or adjust a loan or financial terms. Transaction Risks API This API returns risk data associated with a given transaction. It incorporates various risk factors, including the risk profiles of the involved addresses (both sender and receiver) and the risk associated with the smart contract being interacted with. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Evaluating the risk level of transactions occurring on your platform Providing users with risk assessments before they confirm transactions Implementing fraud detection mechanisms Example implementation: Exposure Risk API This API returns the 'risk profile' of a given address. It indicates the level of exposure the address has to risky activities based on its historical transactions, on-chain behavior, and the risk profiles of the assets it holds. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Understanding the overall risk level of a user's wallet Identifying users with high exposure to risky entities or activities Tailoring risk mitigation strategies based on a user's exposure profile Example implementation: Add an UI element so once the user connects their wallet, they’ll be able to see how safe it is (low/medium/safe/safest) directly in your dApp. For example, an infographic “Safety Score: LOW”. Contract Risk API This API analyzes the risk associated with a given smart contract address. It returns data points and risk scores related to the contract's security, potential vulnerabilities, and historical behavior. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Evaluating the safety of smart contracts before interacting with them Providing users with risk assessments of smart contracts Identifying potentially malicious or vulnerable contracts Identifying past behaviour of contract deployer Example Implementation: Flag tokens, NFTs, NFT collections or addresses in your platform with an UI element in the case they are malicious. Let your users know that the address might be malicious and that they should DYOR. We’ve seen the most demand coming from exchanges, swaps, bridges, DeFi protocols and launchpads. URL Risk This API analyzes the safety of a given URL. It determines if the URL is associated with phishing scams, malware distribution, or other malicious activities. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Protecting users from phishing attacks by identifying malicious URLs Scanning URLs before allowing users to navigate to them within your application Identifying and blocking known malicious websites Common use case: Quest and SocialFi platforms integrate URL Risk API to check/block/track/limit if any URL/link their users post is malicious/drainer/phishing. Holder Analysis API (Invite Only Endpoint) This API provides detailed analysis of the early holders of a specific token. It returns data points related to the distribution of the token among early adopters, identifying potential risks associated with concentrated ownership or suspicious early activity. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Conducting due diligence on new tokens Identifying potential risks related to token distribution Providing insights into the early dynamics of a token's ownership Example implementation: AI Agents or trading bots highlighting high bundling or sniping as an issue and not interacting with a potential rug-pull. Highlighting bundling/sniping history prior to a swap.  ️ How it works Submit the application form (won’t take more than 10 minutes!). Wait for 72 hours to hear back with a decision. If approved, you'll receive an email notification for onboarding and further steps.  Guidelines Be concise & precise: Being clear and concise is always helpful. Bonus points if the application contains well-defined technical details (wherever required). Don’t hesitate to contact us to amend or edit your requirements: Beyond what is specified, if you have any unique insight regarding what your current needs are, feel free to reach out to us info@webacy.com.  Do your homework: Read our API docs, research about Webacy and ask questions if needed. Differentiation: Your application should make it clear how your project is differentiated from other similar projects across relevant ecosystems. Frequently asked questions Where can I read more information about Webacy and its APIs? You can access more information at  https://docs.webacy.com/   What chains do you support? We support Solana, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, BSC, Sei, Sui, Stellar, Ton, and Base. More on the roadmap How much time do I have to integrate?  You have up to 3 months to integrate but the integration agreement should be signed as soon as you are selected as grant winner. Are there any other benefits? Yes, amongst other benefits are co-marketing (access to an audience of over 250,000 unique users) and Webacy PRO access passes for your community or users. Can I whitelabel the frontend UI of the integration? Yes, you can choose whether to add DD.xyz logo/name, or make it completely yours. We can also provide you with a JavaScript snippet which you can copy and paste for the frontend UI. Who is eligible to apply for the grant? Any dApp that supports and is building on Solana, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, BSC, Sei, Ton and Base What criteria will the panelists use to evaluate grants? We prefer projects that 1) yield results quickly 2) are executable by the proposing team. What conditions apply? The only condition is that you periodically update us about the API integration stage and you actively communicate. Will I receive feedback on my proposal if it is rejected? To the best of our abilities given the large volume of submissions.  ️ Apply for the grant now.

name: Statsig Startup Program
description: $50,000 in credits and 1 billion events on the Enterprise tier for 12 months, covering flags, experiments, and analytics together.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: We have received your Startup Program application and will be in touch shortly.
The two criteria to qualify for the Statsig Startup program are:
This program is best for companies with a significant number of users (over 25K MAU) who are scaling fast and need extra event volume.
The startup program is designed for venture-backed companies with a lot of users who are scaling fast.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: If you’re a small startup who’s just getting started, our Developer Tier is the best fit for you needs.
When you need extra events you can always apply for the Startup Program.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: The startup program is designed for venture-backed companies with a lot of users who are scaling fast. If you’re a small startup who’s just getting started, our Developer Tier is the best fit for you needs. When you need extra events you can always apply for the Startup Program.

name: Stellar Foundation - Academic Research Grant
description: Students and researchers can earn academic grants from SDF up to $150,000 in USD. Grants are awarded to research proposals that advance SDF's goals of financial inclusion, fast and inexpensive cross-border payments, efficient decentralized markets, and other beneficial applications of distributed ledger technology.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Stellar Development Foundation is soliciting proposals for scientific, technological, economic, and legal research advancing the foundation’s goals of financial inclusion, fast and inexpensive cross-border payments, efficient decentralized markets, and other beneficial applications of blockchain technology.
Awards will be provided to academic institutions as unrestricted gifts intended to support an individual with PI status.
The funds are intended to support the cost of one graduate student or one post-doc for 12 months, plus reasonable expenses such as conference travel.

To qualify, your institution must be a degree-granting institution whose primary mission is research or higher education, and your institution must be able to confirm that you are authorized to lead research (PI status).

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: Students, consultants, for-profit businesses, and other institutions that do not grant degrees are not eligible.
Awards are paid to academic institutions only and never to individuals.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Privacy-preserving technology, including improvements to both efficiency and regulatory compliance of private payments
Formal verification, including verification of smart contracts and distributed systems
Research related to the Federated Byzantine Agreement model
Scalability solutions for order-books and smart-contracts, including deterministic parallel transaction execution
Legal theories and implications surrounding usage of distributed ledgers or decentralized exchanges for physical property and securities
Incentive design for improving financial responsibility, civic engagement, or other behaviors promoting financial security and democracy
One paragraph biography of principal investigator, including their current academic appointment and highlighting relevant research results and/or former students
Statement that the PI is authorized by their institution to submit research proposals and to lead research (i.e. they have PI status)

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Proposals should propose to make novel scientific contributions, and activities such a literature reviews are not in scope (we expect PIs to be experts in the fields of the proposal).

name: Stellar Foundation - Bug Bounty Program
description: The Stellar Bug Bounty Program provides bounties for vulnerabilities and exploits discovered in the Stellar protocol or any of the code in our repos. We recognize the importance of our community and security researchers in helping identify bugs and issues. We encourage responsible disclosure of security vulnerabilities via our bug bounty program described on this page.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Our development team has up to 90 days to implement a fix based on the severity of the report.
Please allow for this process to fully complete before you publicly disclose the vulnerability.
The Stellar Development Foundation has partnered with HackerOne, a trusted bug bounty platform, to ensure reports are handled in a fair and timely manner.
Payouts vary based on the severity and impact of the report.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: Please refer to the HackerOne program policy for the reward scale and severity classification.
Identify vulnerabilities in the Stellar protocol and core, SDF-maintained repositories and services, and stellar.org web properties.

sections.heading: What gets funded
bullets: Try to include as much information in your report as you can, including a description of the bug, its potential -impact, and steps for reproducing it or proof of concept
Please allow 3 business days for us to respond before sending another email
Implementation bugs that can lead to financial loss
Crash bug in Stellar Core or Horizon (ex. a bug that can crash the app by sending a special request, not by sending thousands requests)
Vulnerabilities on sites hosted by third parties unless they lead to a vulnerability on the main website

description: Audiences Post, Communities Host TL;DR: All our feeds are cooked and touching grass with friends is the final defense. The Superteam touching grass fund is here to support members who host, not just post. Get up to $500 USDG to cover expenses for organizing Solana & Superteam adjacent meet-ups in your city, as per the guidelines below.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Audiences Post, Communities Host TL;DR: All our feeds are cooked and touching grass with friends is the final defense.
The Superteam touching grass fund is here to support members who host, not just post.
Get up to $500 USDG to cover expenses for organizing Solana & Superteam adjacent meet-ups in your city, as per the guidelines below.
Social media platforms are no longer social.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: By default, you don't see content from your friends, family, or people you're connected with.

Instead, our feeds are dominated by sophisticated professionals who are engineering content to elicit a dopamine response while competing for max share of our attention that they can then package and sell to sponsors.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs:
Audiences Post, Communities Host TL;DR: All our feeds are cooked and touching grass with friends is the final defense.
The Superteam touching grass fund is here to support members who host, not just post.
Get up to $500 USDG to cover expenses for organizing Solana & Superteam adjacent meet-ups in your city, as per the guidelines below.
Social media platforms are no longer social.
By default, you don't see content from your friends, family, or people you're connected with.
Instead, our feeds are dominated by sophisticated professionals who are engineering content to elicit a dopamine response while competing for max share of our attention that they can then package and sell to sponsors.
In such times, IRL events are the last defense to compete with brainrot.
Audiences post, communities host: A big focus for each Superteam is to be the frontier onboarding vehicle for the most promising talent in their local markets.
However, the magic happens when members go from sharing memes in a group chat to forming teams on Solana, and often forge lifelong friendships in the process.
The optimal way to participate in Superteam is to use the access & trust from being a member to find your niche interest and the people you can collaborate with to create weekend projects, products, or companies around it.
Those who do it right will find themselves in more group chats than they can count, spontaneously joining Zoom calls and taking cabs/trains/planes to meet their internet friends.
More on this idea in a previous blog post here.
Therefore, Superteam now supports the Solana Foundation community grants program and recommends applicants with the ability to galvanize the community with in-person events for community grants.
Members are encouraged to host casual events like coffee mixers, dinners, paddle or pickleball tournaments, turf football or cricket, or more structured events like learning groups, weekend hackathons, bounty hunting, or co-working sessions.
As long as you're doing something that (a) brings the Solana community closer together and (b) onboards those on the sidelines into crypto, feel free to apply.
Currently, only Superteam members can be hosts, but anyone can attend.
If this format works, we will drop the host restriction and open it up to anyone in the Superteam ecosystem. Events Playbook The meetups are supposed to be a lot of fun, but it's not all there is to a valuable meetup.
To have a higher chance of success—and to get more from the touching grass fund down the line—we recommend doing as many of these as possible: Limited attendees: Invite a small group of not more than 8–10 people.
Focus on a size and venue that enables everyone to talk to everyone else at least once.
A generic meetup isn't the best fit for this; we're only looking to support meetups where attendees are: developers, operators (marketing, product, ops), creators (writers, researchers, YouTubers, etc.), investors (both angels and VCs), founders, and capital markets professionals.
Primer on crypto: Depending on how much is necessary, help folks find their way into the Superteam and Solana ecosystem.
Make them feel at home!
Merch (optional): Coordinate with your local Superteam team to get merch—T-shirts, stickers, bags, etc.—for attendees to take back as a souvenir.
Food & Coffee: If this is part of your event, an ideal meal is one where (1) everyone can talk to each other, and (2) it's reasonably priced and prudently ordered without wasting food or money.
Onboarding: If you're inviting people who are new to crypto or Solana, ideally you should also act as their buddy & help them find their pathway to contribution via bounties, gigs, jobs, hackathons, asset onboarding/distribution, etc.
Proof of meet-up: Ideally, take pictures and put them up on your social media of choice with a short caption sharing your experience, learnings, or thoughts.
Tag your local Superteam as they might share it as well!
This way you can stay in touch and help make more plans that were discussed at dinner!
What this grant is not for: Events that are purely social or personal with no direct link to Solana or Superteam goals.
Misuse of funds or falsified reports can potentially result in being purged from the Superteam membership. ️ How It Works Create a private event page on Luma.
Please ensure you've added an appropriate title, cover image, and a full description of the event — including the format of the event, schedule if any, who the event is for, outcomes for the event, etc.
Make a grant application for it here on Earn, and include the private Luma link of your event in the application.
Sponsors will usually reply within ~7 days.
If approved, you'll receive a confirmation email.
Once approved: Submit your event to the  Superteam Calendar  so it's visible to the broader community.
You'll receive 50% of the grant upfront (post KYC; to be done on this page on Earn) in the following weekly payout cycle.
Approved KYC and payments are sent for processing on Mondays and paid to you by Friday of the same week.
After the event, upload photos from the event + scanned copies of expense receipts from the event to the tranche application form on this listing.
This tranche application form will be visible to you after you have received your first tranche.
Both the photos from the event and scanned copies of the receipts are essential for processing your second tranche. Frequently Asked Questions Who is eligible to apply for event grants?
This program is currently in beta and only open for Superteam Members.
What criteria will the panelists use to evaluate grants?
We prefer to support members that have some prior experience in organizing events (regardless of how small) and events that are primarily focused on developers, artists, and investors.
Will I receive feedback on my proposal if it is rejected?
Unfortunately, our sponsors do not have the bandwidth to provide individualized feedback at this time.   Note: Getting approved for a grant is in no way to be understood as an endorsement or partnership.
Your event will be a community event, and in no way should you represent to third parties that it's a "Superteam event" or in any sense official.   Have a question that isn't answered here?  Email us at support@superteam.fun  for help.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: XRP Ledger's next phase of growth is being built by many, funded by many.
Here's our part.
The XRP Ledger ecosystem is entering a new phase.

Over $550 million has been invested in the XRP Ledger ecosystem since 2017, and the model is shifting: toward a distributed network of independent organizations, each supporting builders in their own way.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: XRPL Commons is one of those pillars.

Since 2023, we've run The Aquarium, an incubator for MVP-stage projects on the XRP Ledger, trained hundreds of developers, and launched the Glow retroactive funding program for open-source contributors.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Glow now runs on a quarterly cadence: open applications, no referral required. The program is 60% disbursed and runs through December 2026. → Apply to Glow

The Aquarium is a 9-week incubation program launched in 2023. Initially run out of Paris, the program is transitioning to online for wider accessibility. It supports developers and founders building within the XRP Ledger ecosystem, providing hands-on mentorship, technical guidance, and direct access to the XRPL Commons team and network. For a selection of projects, this is followed by a 90-day online sprint to unlock growth. Aquarium alumni get priority access to our Early Stage Grants. → Apply to The Aquarium

name: Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)
description: The Zcash Community Grants program funds independent teams entering the Zcash ecosystem, to perform major ongoing development (or other work) for the public good of the Zcash ecosystem.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Zcash Community Grants program (formerly known as ZOMG) funds independent teams entering the Zcash ecosystem, to perform major ongoing development (or other work) for the public good of the Zcash ecosystem.
Funding for Zcash Community Grants comes from the Major Grants slice of the Zcash Dev Fund.
Grants are chosen by a five-person committee elected by the Zcash Community.

ZIP-1014, ZIP-1015&ZIP-1016 were approved by the Zcash community, allocating 8% of mining rewards to provide sustained major grant funding for the ecosystem through the third halving in November 2028.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: This wishlist is meant to encourage ideas for potential applicants to improve the Zcash ecosystem and is not exhaustive.
If your idea to improve Zcash doesn’t fit exactly, feel free to surprise us with your proposal!

name: Zealynx Audit Grants
description: The Zealynx Audit Grants program provides subsidized and fully funded security audits to qualifying Web3 protocols. Applications are evaluated on protocol merit, team strength, and engagement with our security tooling. $100,000+ in audit grants

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Zealynx Audit Grants subsidize or fully fund smart contract audits for Web3 protocols that demonstrate user impact and responsive security practices.
Applications are judged on protocol merit, team experience, and willingness to remediate findings before mainnet expansion.
Final reports are shared with grantees under NDA until critical issues are resolved, then summary results may be published with team consent.

sections.heading: What reviewers expect
bullets: Clear scope covering contracts that custody or route user funds.
Public code repositories and deployment addresses for the version under review.
Remediation commitment for critical and high severity findings prior to wide release.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Complete the Zealynx grants form with architecture diagrams, timelines, and prior audit history if any. Award size may range from partial subsidies to full audits depending on complexity and ecosystem benefit.
Proposals are evaluated by technical committees on a bi-weekly cycle. Funding disbursements are tied to verifiable milestones such as testnet deployment, security review, and mainnet launch.

name: ZetaChain Ecosystem Grants
description: ZetaChain’s milestone-based grants program backs omnichain and Bitcoin-connected dApps, with funding disbursed after reviewers approve scope, milestones, and ecosystem impact.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The public grants program allocates millions of dollars to teams deploying on ZetaChain mainnet, with additional carve-outs for Bitcoin-focused infrastructure, DeFi, and gaming experiments highlighted in ecosystem blog posts.
Both existing projects migrating to ZetaChain and new teams in ideation may apply when intake is open.
Blog posts describe Bitcoin ecosystem tranches and omnichain app priorities; confirm the active intake form before submitting legacy L1-only proposals.

sections.heading: Eligibility
bullets: Deploy audited or review-ready contracts on ZetaChain mainnet and publish addresses plus open-source repositories.
Operate as a legal entity and accept ZetaChain Terms of Use for disbursement.
Use funds for development, liquidity, adoption, or awareness aligned with published milestone agreements.
Demonstrated commitment to open-source licensing (MIT or Apache 2.0) with clean repository documentation and automated test suites.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Submit the Google Form linked from ZetaChain developer grants materials. After screening, the team schedules an intro call, signs an agreement, and receives tranches as milestones complete.
